season_storylines: Patrick Mahomes is rehabbing from knee surgery (Week 15 injury) and is reportedly on track for Week 1, and the market already prices a Chiefs bounce-back from their 6-win 2025 (win total over 10.5), so his 6-pt-passing-TD ceiling is buyable but demands a contingency plan.

San Francisco's receiving corps is decimated - Ricky Pearsall out for the season (PCL), George Kittle on PUP off a January Achilles tear but targeting Week 1, Brandon Aiyuk unavailable, newly signed Mike Evans (quad) and Christian Kirk (calf) banged up - which drags Brock Purdy and makes late-round SF pass catchers pure lottery tickets.

Defending champion Seattle saw its win total slashed from 14 wins to 10.5 after losing Kenneth Walker III and Boye Mafe, opening a near-immediate workhorse path for rookie RB Jadarian Price while Rashid Shaheed doubles as the league's most valuable returner (~90 combined return yards per game) in return-yardage formats.

A massive coaching carousel reshapes fantasy value: Kevin Stefanski's run-heavy scheme lands in Atlanta (Bijan Robinson, Kyle Pitts), Todd Monken in Cleveland, Klint Kubiak's RB-friendly system in Las Vegas (Ashton Jeanty), Mike McCarthy in Pittsburgh, John Harbaugh/Matt Nagy with the Giants, Robert Saleh/Brian Daboll in Tennessee, Mike LaFleur in Arizona, and Jeff Hafley/Bobby Slowik in Miami.

Legal and discipline clouds are unresolved on three relevant names - Josh Jacobs faces open domestic-violence-related charges with a possible conduct-policy ban, Rashee Rice served jail time for a probation violation after a May THC positive with no new NFL ruling yet, and Puka Nacua entered a rehab facility in April with suspension risk still murky (verify) - so all three carry missed-games risk their price may not reflect.

Veteran WR relocation wave moved TD equity around the league: Mike Evans and Deebo Samuel to San Francisco, DK Metcalf drawing Mike McCarthy target design in Pittsburgh, A.J. Brown catching TDs from Drake Maye in New England, and DJ Moore reuniting with Joe Brady in Buffalo as the primary option.

Miami tore it down - Tyreek Hill released in February (still lacking power in his surgically repaired leg as a free agent) and Jaylen Waddle gone - leaving Malik Washington as the de facto WR1 at a WR80 price while De'Von Achane suddenly faces every-down competition from Ollie Gordon under new coach Jeff Hafley.

Malik Nabers is on track for Week 1 after an ACL tear plus a scar-tissue cleanup procedure, making him one of the few discounted elite yardage-and-TD wideouts if camp reports stay clean, with dual-threat Jaxson Dart (QB13 as a rookie) raising the whole Giants passing game under Harbaugh/Nagy.

Rookie RB workloads are unusually clear for August: No. 3 overall pick Jeremiyah Love steps straight into Arizona's lead role, Jadarian Price inherits Seattle's backfield, and Bhayshul Tuten takes over Jacksonville after Travis Etienne's exit - goal-line-inclusive roles that are gold at 10 yards per point with zero PPR dilution.

Betting markets peg New England (over 9.5), the Rams, Chiefs, Eagles and 49ers (all 10.5+) as the top environments, while Arizona and Miami sit at 4.5 wins - meaning negative game scripts that suppress TD equity for Cardinals and Dolphins skill players outside their alpha touch-getters.

teams.outlook: New HC Mike LaFleur brings a McVay-style scheme but the league-low 4.5 win total means trailing scripts; No. 3 pick Jeremiyah Love's immediate lead-back role and Marvin Harrison Jr.'s downfield TD equity are the plays, with rookie QB Carson Beck impressing in camp (verify).

Kevin Stefanski installs a run-heavy, featured-back scheme that makes Bijan Robinson a consensus top pick and revives Kyle Pitts as a top-12 TE bet, while Michael Penix Jr. manages a knee issue that caps stacking appeal.

A rebuilt staff under HC Jesse Minter with Mike McDaniel calling the offense is expected to feature Justin Herbert and Omarion Hampton (verify), and with Isaiah Likely gone Mark Andrews should recapture enough red-zone targets to stay a TE1.

Joe Brady was promoted to head coach and imported DJ Moore as the primary option in an offense he already knows, keeping Buffalo's six-straight-years-over-10.5-wins environment intact and Moore a discounted yardage-and-TD WR2.

Kenny Pickett starts the Hall of Fame Game amid an unsettled QB picture (verify), and the backfield is the real story - Jonathon Brooks' return threatens Chuba Hubbard's workload, making Hubbard a fade at his current price.

Chicago faces the league's toughest schedule, but second-year Luther Burden III is set for a target spike with DJ Moore gone, while RB Kyle Monangai (day-to-day, soft tissue) offers little receiving utility and is script-dependent.

The Bengals draw the league's easiest schedule and a win total of over 9.5 that implies real improvement, keeping their passing-game core in the top pricing tier and making TE Erick All Jr. (finally healthy after knee procedures) a free dart.

Todd Monken's arrival features RB and TE usage - Quinshon Judkins (five double-digit fantasy games) and Harold Fannin Jr. are the beneficiaries - but the QB battle remains genuinely unsettled (verify), and the easiest-schedule tier softens game-script risk.

Javonte Williams returns off a 1,201-yard, 11-TD season; the national fade case is his empty receiving line, which matters far less in non-PPR, though TD regression from 11 scores is the real risk to price in, with Ryan Flournoy a deep injury-contingent WR stash.
Bo Nix finished as the QB7 yet is being drafted around QB15, and his rushing floor plus low INT rate makes him a screaming value in a 6-pt-passing-TD, -2 INT format.

Jared Goff has averaged 17+ points per game and is priced at QB16, a clean high-TD low-INT value in this scoring, while Brian Branch's Achilles rehab (unlikely before December) mainly dents the defense.

Josh Jacobs carries open legal risk with a possible conduct-policy suspension, Tucker Kraft is off PUP and practicing after his ACL tear, and deep threat Christian Watson is the profile this league rewards - big plays and TDs over catch volume.
Jayden Higgins is locked in as the No. 2 behind Nico Collins with coaching praise, while Tank Dell's knee remains a monitor - Houston's vertical passing tree suits yardage-per-point scoring.

The Michael Pittman trade funnels targets to Josh Downs, but his slot-compiler profile loses most of its edge at zero PPR - deep threat Alec Pierce (ankle, expected off PUP shortly) is the better fit for this format's yardage-and-TD scoring.

Travis Etienne's departure hands Bhayshul Tuten a significant workload with goal-line access, and Travis Hunter is fully cleared from his LCL tear but will play primarily corner with only a receiver rotation role.

Mahomes is on track for Week 1 off knee surgery with the market pricing a bounce-back (over 10.5 wins); Xavier Worthy is healthy, locked into the No. 2 role and undervalued, while Rashee Rice's probation situation leaves suspension risk unresolved.
Tre Harris enters Year 2 as a starter and is going essentially undrafted despite a guaranteed expanded role, though the offense's post-shakeup identity and QB situation remain murky (verify).

The Rams carry a top-tier over 10.5 win total, but Puka Nacua's April rehab stint leaves lingering suspension uncertainty (verify) - Davante Adams and Kyren Williams absorb the TD equity if he misses time, with Blake Corum (5.1 YPC) the premium handcuff.

Klint Kubiak's featured-back scheme is built for Ashton Jeanty to improve on his RB11 finish and keeps Brock Bowers central, with Kirk Cousins starting ahead of rookie Fernando Mendoza on a 5.5-win team whose scripts cap the passing ceiling.

New coach Jeff Hafley and OC Bobby Slowik inherit a stripped roster (4.5 win total) - Malik Washington is the last target hog standing at a WR80 price, but De'Von Achane now faces every-down competition from Ollie Gordon and Malik Willis at QB caps the passing game (verify).
Kyler Murray is the clear camp winner at QB (verify) and has finished top-10 in four of five seasons - his rushing ceiling plus 6-pt passing TDs makes him a bargain at cost in this format.

The Patriots carry a near-league-best over 9.5 win total; A.J. Brown (playing through a dislocated thumb) is stacking TDs with Drake Maye, TreVeyon Henderson (5.1 YPC) pushes Rhamondre Stevenson, and D'Ernest Johnson/Marcus Jones add sneaky return-yardage points.
Tyler Shough closed his rookie year strong and got supporting-cast help, and the Saints sit in the league's easiest-schedule tier, making the whole offense modestly undervalued in TD-based scoring.

John Harbaugh with Matt Nagy's heavy 12/13 personnel elevates Theo Johnson, Cam Skattebo is the established RB1 being drafted around RB20 with bellcow potential, and dual-threat Jaxson Dart plus a Week-1-tracking Malik Nabers give the passing game real TD upside.
A 5.5-win rebuild limits scoring environment, but OC Frank Reich's TE track record makes first-TE-drafted Kenyon Sadiq the one Jets piece with format-friendly red-zone equity.
Philadelphia sits in the top betting tier at over 10.5 wins with its core intact, and rookie Makai Lemon has a path to the No. 2 WR job with a high ceiling despite a crowded room (verify).

Mike McCarthy's historically fantasy-friendly offense funnels TD-zone targets to DK Metcalf, splits a quality backfield between Jaylen Warren, Kenneth Gainwell and bargain signing Rico Dowdle (back-to-back 1,000-yard seasons), and rookie Drew Allar is impressing in camp.

The defending champs' win total fell from 14 to 10.5 after losing Kenneth Walker III, handing rookie Jadarian Price a weekly-starter role, with Zach Charbonnet on PUP (knee) and Rashid Shaheed delivering elite return-yardage points on top of his WR role.

A 10.5-win-caliber roster with a shattered receiving corps - Pearsall out for the year, Kittle (Achilles) racing for Week 1 off PUP, Aiyuk unavailable, Evans and Kirk nicked - makes Purdy a fade at cost and De'Zhaun Stribling/Jake Tonges free upside.

Mike Evans' departure clears the alpha role for sophomore Emeka Egbuka (managing minor soreness), whose downfield-and-red-zone profile fits non-PPR perfectly, with Jalen McMillan the secondary beneficiary.

Robert Saleh with Brian Daboll calling plays should stabilize Year 2 Cam Ward, but rookie Carnell Tate's top-60 price demands immediate elite production behind an established slot presence - Elic Ayomanor, Chimere Dike and TE Gunnar Helm (44 rookie catches, Okonkwo gone) are the cheaper routes.

Rachaad White joins a thin backfield as the pass-catching back, but his 3.9 career YPC and a Jayden Daniels-centric run game cap him hard in a format where his receptions are worth zero - Daniels' rushing keeps him a premium QB.

breakout_watch.name: Jeremiyah Love
breakout_watch.why: No. 3 overall pick walking into Arizona's lead-back job with goal-line access from day one - immediate workload plus TD equity is exactly what non-PPR pays for.

breakout_watch.name: Cam Skattebo
breakout_watch.why: Established as the Giants' clear RB1 in camp yet still drafted around RB20; Harbaugh/Nagy's heavy-personnel run game gives him bellcow carries and short-yardage TDs.

breakout_watch.name: TreVeyon Henderson
breakout_watch.why: 5.1 yards per rush as a rookie in the league's best-priced offense (Patriots over 9.5 wins); a Year 2 leap past Stevenson means efficient yardage plus scores.

breakout_watch.name: Quinshon Judkins
breakout_watch.why: Todd Monken's RB-featuring scheme plus five double-digit fantasy games already banked; Cleveland's easiest-tier schedule supports positive scripts.

breakout_watch.name: Bhayshul Tuten
breakout_watch.why: Travis Etienne's exit leaves him positioned for a significant Jacksonville workload including the goal line - a volume-and-TD role at a modest price.

breakout_watch.name: Ashton Jeanty
breakout_watch.why: Klint Kubiak's featured-back system arrives to smooth out an RB11 finisher; more designed touches and red-zone work raise his weekly floor and ceiling.

breakout_watch.name: Jadarian Price
breakout_watch.why: Kenneth Walker III is gone and Charbonnet opened camp on PUP - the rookie is positioned as a weekly starter on the defending champs.

breakout_watch.name: Emeka Egbuka
breakout_watch.why: Mike Evans' departure removes the target and red-zone competition; sophomore alpha role with downfield usage that beats slot volume in zero-PPR.

breakout_watch.name: Luther Burden III
breakout_watch.why: Expected second-year target spike with DJ Moore gone from Chicago; his after-catch yardage converts directly at 10 yards per point.

breakout_watch.name: Christian Watson
breakout_watch.why: Strong close to last season and reduced receiving competition in Green Bay; a deep-threat TD-maker whose profile is exactly what non-PPR rewards over compilers.

breakout_watch.name: Jayden Higgins
breakout_watch.why: Locked into Houston's No. 2 role behind Nico Collins with coaching praise, in a vertical offense that produces chunk yardage and end-zone shots.

breakout_watch.name: Xavier Worthy
breakout_watch.why: Healthy from the shoulder issue and locked into the Chiefs' No. 2 job with Mahomes tracking for Week 1 - discounted speed-and-TD upside in a bounce-back offense.

breakout_watch.name: Jaxson Dart
breakout_watch.why: QB13 as a rookie averaging 17+ points, dual-threat legs, and star receivers returning - rushing yardage plus 6-pt passing TDs give him a top-8 ceiling at a mid-round cost.

breakout_watch.name: Rashid Shaheed
breakout_watch.why: League's top returner at roughly 90 combined return yards per game (about 4-5 extra points weekly at 20 yds/pt) stacked on a real deep-threat WR role in Seattle - a unique floor-raiser in this format.

fade_watch.name: Chuba Hubbard
fade_watch.why: Jonathon Brooks' return from ACL rehab threatens the workload split in Carolina; a top-72 price for a possibly shared backfield with reduced goal-line certainty.

fade_watch.name: Rashee Rice
fade_watch.why: Probation violation (May THC positive) after a jail stint leaves NFL discipline unresolved - suspension risk isn't priced in, and his catch-volume profile is less valuable at zero PPR anyway.

fade_watch.name: Josh Jacobs
fade_watch.why: Open domestic-violence-related charges carry realistic conduct-policy suspension risk (up to 6 games if convicted); drafting him at his usual RB1 price ignores multi-week downside.

fade_watch.name: Brock Purdy
fade_watch.why: His receiving corps is decimated (Pearsall out for the year, Kittle on PUP, Aiyuk unavailable, Evans/Kirk hurt); fewer passing TDs and more risk-forced INTs at -2 make him a fade at cost.

fade_watch.name: Carnell Tate
fade_watch.why: A top-60 pick price requires immediate elite production from a rookie behind established slot target Wan'Dale Robinson with a still-developing Cam Ward at QB.

fade_watch.name: Josh Downs
fade_watch.why: The Pittman trade boosts his targets, but he's a short-area slot compiler - in a zero-PPR, 10-yards-per-point league his added catches are worth nothing without yardage and TDs.

fade_watch.name: Rachaad White
fade_watch.why: Career 3.9 YPC between the tackles and a role built on receptions that score zero in this format, inside a Washington offense that funnels goal-line value to Jayden Daniels.

fade_watch.name: Kyle Monangai
fade_watch.why: Poor receiving efficiency (60% catch rate, 5.5 yards per target) makes him game-script dependent, he's already nursing a soft-tissue injury, and Chicago faces the league's hardest schedule.

uncertainty_note: The biggest open questions right now: NFL discipline is unresolved for Josh Jacobs, Rashee Rice, and Puka Nacua (any ruling instantly reprices all three); Week 1 availability is still projection not fact for Patrick Mahomes (knee), George Kittle (Achilles), Malik Nabers (ACL/scar tissue), and Tucker Kraft (ACL); several QB rooms (Cleveland, Carolina, and the Chargers' post-shakeup situation) are genuinely unsettled; and some reported offseason relocations in a chaotic carousel (e.g., Justin Herbert and Omarion Hampton to Baltimore, Kyler Murray to Minnesota) rest on single-source summaries and should be re-verified before roster-altering moves.
